packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING - packet-11

Exposure statement: no outside source, catalogue, edition or earlier transcription was consulted. No
identification of work or author is attempted. (Process note: one directory listing of the packet folders was
run to see image filenames; packet.json was not opened.) Names that appear below (e.g. "greg", "aug", "iob",
"lu") are transcribed from the letters on the fragment itself as its own citations.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001 = overview of one side (side 1) of a narrow vertical parchment strip, roughly 7 x 17 cm by the ruler;
  image-006 = overview of the other side (side 2). Images 002-005 are details of side 1, 007-010 of side 2.
- The strip is a single column's width or less: on side 1 the left edge cuts into line-beginnings and the right
  edge into line-ends; on side 2 the left edge is cut/abraded (beginnings lost) and the right edge cuts line-ends.
  So no line is certainly complete. About 45 lines per side. Whether the leaf originally had one or two columns
  cannot be told from this crop.
- Very small, rapid, extremely abbreviated cursive hand, brown ink. No rubrics, no colour, no running title seen.
  Upper margin of side 1 carries a short isolated word in a different, larger hand ("holo(n)"? / "kolon"? -
  not read securely).
- Side 2 has one clearly enlarged, pen-flourished initial "I" (image-008 L7) with paraph-like strokes, opening
  a new unit; elsewhere small paraph-like marks ("p(re)t(erea)" with a looped sign) separate arguments.
- Side 1 is heavily rubbed and stained in the middle third; side 2 is clearer.
- Tentative interpretation only: disputation-style prose (objections each introduced by "p(re)t(erea)" with a
  cited authority and book/chapter number, then responses "ad 1 ... ad 2 ... dic(endum)"). Side 2 concerns
  where souls are located ("sinus abrahe", "limbus", "infernus"); side 1 has vocabulary of appetite/will
  ("appetit(us)", "uelle", "uolu(n)tas", "deformitas"). Not interpreted further.

SPANS SELECTED
Side 2 upper half, lines 3-19 (images 007 and 008; image-008 L1-L2 repeat image-007 L10-L11), plus scattered
lines lower on side 2 (image-009, image-010). Side 1: only disjointed phrases could be read (images 002-005);
given as fragments, not as connected text. Unread: most of side 1; the lowest ten lines of side 2.

LIMITATIONS
- This is the least secure of my packets: the hand is a tiny abbreviated cursive and the strip truncates every
  line. On side 2 the recurring words sinus abrahe / limbus / infernus / locus / pena / puerorum are clear; the
  citation numerals (13, 14, 16, 20, "1a") are read from small figures and may be wrong.
- "g°" is read as (ergo); "p(re)t(erea)" is the expansion proposed for the looped sign that opens arguments.
- Side 1 lines are isolated phrases with gaps; do not treat them as continuous.
- Which side is recto, and where the strip sat in its original leaf, cannot be determined from the images.
- A higher-resolution or raking/UV image of side 1 would be needed for any connected reading.
